Burden by block for each structural traversal of the survey

Source: R/path_burden_traversals.R
path_burden_traversals.Rd

path_burden_profile() returns each route's burden distribution as a total. This function returns the traversals behind it: one row per traversal and block, with points, items, response items and pages, so that burden can be accumulated through the survey from the same weighted traversals as the total.

Usage

path_burden_traversals(
  qsf,
  method = c("auto", "exact", "sample"),
  n_draws = 10000L,
  seed = 1L,
  loop_weights = NULL,
  field_rules = NULL,
  complete_only = TRUE,
  scheme = gfs_scheme(),
  max_paths = 10000L,
  max_traversals = 1e+05,
  overrides = NULL,
  choice_tasks = NULL,
  field_domains = NULL,
  respect_force_response = TRUE,
  output = c("long", "wide", "summary"),
  probs = c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1),
  chunk = 10000L
)

Arguments

qsf

A qsf_raw object or a path accepted by read_qsf().

method

"auto", "exact" or "sample".

n_draws

Traversals sampled per route.

seed

Random seed for sampling. The global random-number state is restored afterwards.

loop_weights

Optional named list of loop-count weights, keyed by Loop & Merge block id: a non-negative numeric vector with one weight per iteration count 1..max (normalised internally), or a function of the component's shared-gate states returning such a vector. NULL (default) weights each count equally, e.g. list(BL_x = c(1, 1, 1, 9)).

field_rules

Optional named list of derivation rules (see Details).

complete_only

Only routes that complete the survey (default).

scheme

A gfs_scheme() list.

max_paths

Passed to resolve_paths().

max_traversals

Largest number of traversals per route that "exact" enumerates.

overrides

Optional named numeric vector of GfS+ points that replace the computed score of the named questions, e.g. c(QID51 = 10). See burden_report(). Ignored, with a warning, when engine is supplied.

choice_tasks

Optional data frame declaring stated-choice tasks (question_id, n_alternatives, n_attributes), scored by the GfS stated-choice rule. See burden_report(). Ignored, with a warning, when engine is supplied.

field_domains

Optional named list giving the values an embedded-data field can hold, e.g. list(SP_05 = 0:5). Passed to resolve_flow(). Ignored, with a warning, when engine is supplied.

respect_force_response

If TRUE (default), a display-logic trigger that the route shows and whose response is forced (ForceResponse = "ON") has no unanswered state, when its referenced choices cover all its choices. FALSE gives the 0.2.0 behaviour.

output

"long" (one row per traversal and route block), "wide" (one row per traversal, one points column per survey block) or "summary" (weighted quantiles only; draws are not kept).

probs

Quantile probabilities for output = "summary".

chunk

Draws simulated at a time when sampling.

Value

For "long", a tibble with traversal_id, path_id, weight, block_id, flow_order (the block's position in the survey flow), iterations (NA outside loops), points, items, response_items and pages. For "summary", a list with totals (weighted quantiles of the traversal totals of points, response items and pages) and cumulative (weighted quantiles of points accumulated through the survey's blocks in flow order; blocks a route skips add zero). All outputs carry attributes method, rejected, unresolved, seed, n_draws and convention.

Details

A traversal walks a route in flow order. A question is shown if the route always shows it, or if its display logic holds given the answers drawn so far. A trigger question gets a state only when it is shown: hidden means unanswered; shown with a forced response (ForceResponse = "ON", when respect_force_response = TRUE) means answered; otherwise answered or unanswered. Each state of a trigger, and each iteration count of a Loop & Merge block (loop_weights, equal by default), is a branch. Inside a loop, triggers in the same block are drawn afresh in each iteration; other triggers keep one state.

Weights. Every route has equal total weight. With method = "exact" every branch combination is enumerated and weighted by the product of its branch weights, so the weights reproduce the structural convention of path_burden_profile(). With method = "sample", n_draws traversals are drawn per route (stratified by route), each with weight 1 / (n_routes * n_draws). "auto" enumerates when the number of traversals is at most max_traversals, and samples otherwise. The method used per route is in attr(x, "method"). These are model weights, not observed frequencies.

Derived fields. field_rules derives stored fields from the answers drawn in a traversal, for values that survey code (for example page JavaScript) computes and the survey file does not record. Each element, named by its target ("@Field" for a stored field, "@n:<BL_id>" for a loop's iteration count), is a function of the traversal state, or list(fun = , inputs = ) naming questions the rule reads that are not display-logic triggers (these are then drawn when shown: every choice, plus unanswered unless forced). In the state, a loop question's answer in iteration j is "<QID>#<j>" and a loop count is "@n:<BL_id>". A derived field is never enumerated; its value is set before any display logic that reads it. A rule returning NA rejects the traversal: exact weights are renormalised within the route, rejected draws are redrawn, and the rejected share per route is in attr(x, "rejected"). A loop-count rule makes routes that contain its loop sampled (loop_weights for that loop are then ignored, with a warning). A display condition that reads a question later in the flow is listed in attr(x, "unresolved") as a forward reference; that question is read as unanswered.

Speed. A rule is called once per distinct combination of its inputs, and results are reused across chunks and routes. Rules with many inputs (for example an answer in each of ten loop iterations) are faster when vectorised: list(fun = , inputs = , vectorised = TRUE) calls fun once per chunk with whole columns ("" for unanswered, choice ids otherwise; loop counts as integers, NULL when the route has no such loop) and expects one value per traversal.

Differences from path_burden_profile(): no primary-gate approximation; a conditionally shown forced trigger never has an unanswered state; and field_rules apply. Without these, exact traversal quantiles equal the profile's.

Examples

# \donttest{
q <- read_qsf(system.file("extdata", "demo_travel_survey.qsf",
                          package = "surveyBurden"))
x <- path_burden_traversals(q, method = "exact")
head(x)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 10
#>   traversal_id path_id  weight block_id flow_order iterations points items
#>          <int>   <int>   <dbl> <chr>         <int>      <int>  <dbl> <int>
#> 1            1       3 0.00139 BL1               1         NA     11     1
#> 2            1       3 0.00139 BL2               2         NA      1     1
#> 3            1       3 0.00139 BL3               3         NA      2     1
#> 4            1       3 0.00139 BL4               4         NA     15     5
#> 5            1       3 0.00139 BL5               5         NA      3     2
#> 6            1       3 0.00139 BL6               6          1      4     2
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: response_items <int>, pages <int>
# }
